Two-stage analysis of a multi-location trial, for any design

Source: R/two_stage.R
analyze_two_stage.Rd

Analyses each location on its own (stage 1) and combines the genotype means across locations (stage 2), weighting them by their precision (Möhring and Piepho, 2009). Works for every design of the package grown at several locations: augmented row-column, augmented p-rep and resolvable row-column designs. For augmented p-rep designs, analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage() gives the same analysis with the p-rep block model of the paper.

Usage

analyze_two_stage(
  data,
  response,
  stage1 = c("spatial", "blocks", "design"),
  weighting = c("full", "diagonal", "none"),
  genotype_by_location = c("random", "none"),
  genotype_col = "all_entries",
  location_col = "location",
  row_col = "row",
  col_col = "col",
  replicate_col = NULL,
  block_col = NULL,
  spatial_nseg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with all locations (one row per plot), with the design columns and a response column.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

stage1

"spatial", "blocks" or "design".

weighting

"full", "diagonal" or "none".

genotype_by_location

"random" or "none".

genotype_col, location_col

Genotype and location columns.

row_col, col_col

Field row and column coordinates (spatial stage 1).

replicate_col, block_col

Optional replicate (fixed) and block (random) columns of the spatial stage 1. By default "replicate" and "block" when the data have them.

spatial_nseg

Optional number of P-spline segments, c(col, row).

Value

An object of class two_stage_analysis: a list with adjusted_means (combined, ranked), variance_components, locations (one row per location), heterogeneity (Hartley's Fmax), stage1_means, stage1_fits (per location, with plot_results, for first_stage_values() and compare_first_stage()) and diagnostics.

Stage 1

stage1 = "spatial" (default)

A 'SpATS' spatial model at every location (Rodríguez-Álvarez et al., 2018): genotypes fixed, a smooth two-dimensional P-spline surface over the field rows and columns, replicates fixed and blocks random when replicate_col and block_col are given.

stage1 = "blocks"

A linear model at every location that needs no design object: replicates and blocks within replicates fixed (when replicate_col and block_col are given), genotypes fixed. For data read from Breedbase without field coordinates.

stage1 = "design"

The design's own model at every location: analyze_augmented_row_column_design() for augmented row-column designs, analyze_resolvable_row_column() (row-column model) for resolvable row-column designs, and the block model of analyze_augmented_prep_design() for p-rep designs. The design is recognised from its columns.

The stage-1 genotype means are BLUEs with their full covariance matrix.

Stage 2

As in analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(): fixed locations and genotypes, random genotype-by-location effects (REML), and stage-1 errors with the stage-1 covariance (weighting = "full"), only the stage-1 variances ("diagonal") or a common error ("none", for comparison).

References

Möhring, J. and Piepho, H.-P. (2009). Comparison of weighting in two-stage analysis of plant breeding trials. Crop Science 49, 1977-1988. doi:10.2135/cropsci2009.02.0083

Rodríguez-Álvarez, M. X., Boer, M. P., van Eeuwijk, F. A. and Eilers, P. H. C. (2018). Correcting for spatial heterogeneity in plant breeding experiments with P-splines. Spatial Statistics 23, 52-71. doi:10.1016/j.spasta.2017.10.003

Examples

# The same augmented row-column layout, randomized at three locations.
sites <- c("North", "Central", "South")
trials <- lapply(seq_along(sites), function(i) {
  d <- augmented_row_column_design(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4),
                                   12, 12, 4, 4, n_candidates = 5, seed = i)$design
  d$location <- sites[i]
  d
})
met <- do.call(rbind, trials)
set.seed(1)
g <- stats::setNames(stats::rnorm(112, sd = 3), c(paste0("G", 1:108), paste0("C", 1:4)))
met$yield <- 50 + g[met$all_entries] + 0.5 * met$row + stats::rnorm(nrow(met))
fit <- analyze_two_stage(met, "yield", stage1 = "design")
fit
#> Two-stage analysis
#> Stage 1: design model per location; stage 2: full weighting, genotype x location random
#>

#>     9      G11           3         57.70    0.6273

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("SpATS", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spatial <- analyze_two_stage(met, "yield")      # SpATS at every location
  spatial$locations
}
